descriptor: Operating company · reported in CNY · quoted in HKD

charts.title: Operating Income vs Insurance Revenue (IFRS 17)
charts.annotation: Insurance revenue is only reported FY2022 onward, under IFRS 17; the CSV's GrossWrittenPremiums column is the pre-IFRS17 equivalent (FY2020-FY2021).

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For China Pacific Insurance (Group) Co., Ltd. (CPIC): equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For China Pacific Insurance (Group) Co., Ltd. (CPIC): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For China Pacific Insurance (Group) Co., Ltd. (CPIC): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For China Pacific Insurance (Group) Co., Ltd. (CPIC): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

insuranceRevenue.title: Insurance revenue vs operating income
insuranceRevenue.content:
Insurance revenue is the IFRS 17 "insurance revenue" line -- premiums earned on the insurance-service component of policies, recognised as coverage is provided, net of reinsurance. It excludes investment income and the deposit (savings) component of many life policies, so it runs well below total Revenue (operating income), which also includes net investment income on the ~RMB4tn float and other income.

For China Pacific Insurance (Group) Co., Ltd. (CPIC): the gap between the two lines is CPIC's investment result -- in a weak equity-market year that gap narrows even if underwriting is healthy, and in a strong year it widens. Insurance revenue only exists from FY2022 (IFRS 17 adoption); the pre-2022 equivalent disclosure was Gross Written Premiums (a different, broader measure -- written not earned, and gross of reinsurance).

What to watch:

  • Insurance revenue growth versus total revenue growth -- a widening gap signals investment income is driving results, not underwriting
  • The life (CPIC Life) vs P&C (CPIC P/C) mix within this line, since the two segments price and reserve very differently
  • Interim rows for H1 seasonality before comparing to a full FY

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For China Pacific Insurance (Group) Co., Ltd. (CPIC): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For China Pacific Insurance (Group) Co., Ltd. (CPIC): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For China Pacific Insurance (Group) Co., Ltd. (CPIC): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For China Pacific Insurance (Group) Co., Ltd. (CPIC): the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For China Pacific Insurance (Group) Co., Ltd. (CPIC): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
